title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Summary for the trading session ending Friday, August 15, 2026

items.headline: U.S. Markets Edge Lower on Weak Retail Sales; S&P 500 Secures Third Winning Week
items.summary: U.S. equities pulled back from recent highs on Friday, August 15, 2026, as a weaker-than-expected retail sales report dampened investor sentiment. Despite the daily dip across major indices, the S&P 500 managed to close out its third consecutive winning week. Energy and Cyclicals showed underlying strength amidst broader market caution. Not financial advice.

items.statContext: Slipped 0.2% from its record high. The index closed out its third consecutive winning week.
Declined following concerns over economic data.

items.headline: Reddit Surges on S&P 500 Inclusion News
items.summary: Shares of Reddit ($RDDT) jumped 12.6% after the announcement that the company's stock will be joining the S&P 500 index next Tuesday.

items.headline: Citigroup Leads Financial Sector Gains
items.summary: Citigroup ($C) was among the top financial gainers, adding 3.21% for the week, boosted by strong corporate earnings across the banking industry.

items.headline: Applied Materials Falls Despite Strong Earnings
items.summary: Applied Materials ($AMAT) shares fell 5.1% despite the semiconductor technology company reporting stronger-than-expected profit and revenue for its latest quarter. The decline was attributed to elevated expectations and broader concerns about AI stock valuations.

items.headline: Unexpected Dip in U.S. Retail Sales Raises Economic Concerns
items.summary: A surprising report indicated that U.S. retail sales slipped 0.6% in July, the largest drop since May 2025, as consumers spent less than the previous month. Economists had anticipated continued growth in spending. This data contributed to the cautious market sentiment on Friday.

items.headline: Inflation Cools in July, Producer Prices Jump in August
items.summary: U.S. inflation slowed in July, with consumer prices rising 3.4% year-over-year, slightly down from June's 3.5%. Monthly consumer prices increased a modest 0.1%. However, the Producer Price Index (PPI) surged 0.7% in August, exceeding forecasts, largely due to a 10.5% rise in the energy price index.

items.headline: Fed Holds Rates Steady Amid Dissent, Future Hikes Expected
items.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained its key interest rate at approximately 3.6% at its last meeting, although three officials favored a rate hike. Wall Street generally anticipates at least one more rate hike before the end of 2026. Minutes from the July FOMC meeting, expected next week, will provide further insights into policy discussions.

items.headline: Energy and Commodities Lead with Rising Oil Prices
items.summary: The Energy sector and broader commodities demonstrated significant strength during the week. Crude oil and gasoline prices continued their upward trend, with Brent crude rising 1.7% to $88.52 per barrel, influenced by ongoing geopolitical uncertainties.
